name: Comment
text: Depends on the kind of paint. But in general, with oil and acrylic paint, I use no gloves. Not needed. And sometimes I use my fingers to correct the paint on the canvas and than I need the feeling of the paint. . No worries, I got the perfect hand-wash a mixture of very fine sand and liquid soap. But with more aggressive paint, I do use gloves

name: Comment
text: Sometimes it's not an option. Wallpaper hanging an example.

name: Comment
text: I personally like to make personal contact with what I'm using. Gloves deaden feeling. When I sand, I use my hands to feel for humps. You can't always see them. Gloves will prevent you from feeling the slightest humps. And when you paint those humps, they pop out....

name: Comment
text: I lectured decorating and health and safety for over a decade. I’ve seen bad cases of industrial dermatitis. I wear gloves and I advised all my students to wear gloves. There’s no cure once you get it. Only a fool neglects their skin. You may think it’s sissy and you might think a real man wouldn’t wear them. A real attractive woman won’t let your hands anywhere near her if you’ve got industrial dermatitis
